issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) for SealSaloon to receive ingredient deliveries, but the solution implements this functionality as a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int). This name/signature mismatch is structural: students implementing the class based on the problem statement will expect acceptSupplyDelivery, and automated tests (or graders) that call acceptSupplyDelivery will fail if the method is named differently.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent. Either rename the solution's receiveDelivery method to acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) (keeping the same behavior and static modifier), or update the problem statement and UML to require receiveDelivery(String, int, int). Ensure tests and templates use the same method name.

issues.description: The problem statement and the (template) Main example refer to a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int) on SealSaloon, but the solution implementation provides a static method named receiveDelivery(String, int, int) instead. This inconsistent method name for the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery) will confuse students mapping requirements to code and likely cause test mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across all artifacts. Rename the solution's receiveDelivery method to acceptSupplyDelivery (or add a forwarding acceptSupplyDelivery that calls receiveDelivery) and ensure any example usage (Main) and tests call acceptSupplyDelivery so the problem statement, template, and solution are aligned.
